$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)
$$

Let $F(x)=-2x+3$ for $x\in [0,\pi ).$ The Fourier sine series of the **odd** $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the expression for ${b}_{n}.$$\,{b}_{n}=$ {{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
For our Fourier sine series, the coefficients are given by

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $f(x)=-2x+3$ for $x\in (0,\pi ).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
{b}_{n}=\frac{2}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(-2x+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x.
$$

We use the integration by parts: 

$$
\begin{aligned}u=-2x+3\, & ⇒\,{u}^{′}=-2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\, & ⇒\,v=-\frac{1}{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{b}_{n} & =\frac{2}{\pi }(uv\,{|}_{0}^{\pi }-{\int }_{0}^{\pi }v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x) \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }(-\frac{1}{n}[(-2x+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }-\frac{2}{n}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x) \\  & =-\frac{2}{n\pi }(((-2\pi +3)\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-3\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(0))+\frac{2}{n}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)]_{0}^{\pi }) \\  & =-\frac{2}{n\pi }((-2\pi +3)\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-3+\frac{2}{n}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\pi )-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0))) \\  & =-\frac{2}{n\pi }((-2\pi +3)\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )-3).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\pi )=(-1)^{n},$ we have

$$
{b}_{n}=-\frac{2}{n\pi }((-2\pi +3)(-1)^{n}-3)=\frac{2}{n\pi }((-1)^{n}(2\pi -3)+3).
$$
